item.title: Subtle Handle Watermark Throughout

turns.text: Add @flightschool as a subtle watermark at the bottom right for this whole clip. Small white text, slightly see-through, with a faint shadow so it's still readable. Keep it away from the edges and leave everything else alone.

item.tests: Tests exact handle rendering as a persistent, readable, translucent watermark without changing the source footage or audio.

answer_sheet.Position and timing: Bottom right, inset from both edges, fixed in place throughout all 7 seconds.
answer_sheet.Watermark styling: Small white text, slightly translucent, with a faint shadow. Exact font and opacity are your call.
answer_sheet.Video and audio preservation: Keep the original aspect ratio, framing, complete footage, duration, and sound. Do not add an end card or other graphics.

must_haves: The watermark reads exactly '@flightschool' and stays visible throughout the entire clip.
The handle remains fixed at the bottom right with clear space between the text and both frame edges.
The text is small, white, visibly translucent, and readable against the changing footage, with a subtle shadow.
The original cockpit footage remains unchanged apart from the watermark, with no extra card or scene.
The output lasts 7 seconds and preserves the original synchronized audio.

turns.text: Add @flightschool as a subtle watermark at the bottom right for this whole clip. Small white text, slightly see-through, with a faint shadow so it's still readable. Keep it away from the edges and leave everything else alone. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run or spent credits.** For this edit, the cheapest—and safest—option is a normal text overlay, not AI video editing.

- **Local overlay: 0 Magic Hour credits**, at full length and original resolution.
- **Magic Hour AI editing:** I can’t verify an exact credit quote with the available tools, and it may alter other details or render the handle inaccurately. I wouldn’t use it for “leave everything else alone.”

I don’t have a standard watermark-overlay tool connected here, so I can’t directly produce the exact edit for you. If you have **FFmpeg** installed, download the clip as `radio-lines.mp4` and run:

```bash
ffmpeg -i radio-lines.mp4 -vf "drawtext=text='@flightschool':fontsize=h*0.025:fontcolor=white@0.65:shadowcolor=black@0.3:shadowx=1:shadowy=1:x=w-tw-w*0.04:y=h-th-h*0.04" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset medium -c:a copy radio-lines-watermarked.mp4
```

This adds small, 65%-opaque white text with a faint shadow, inset 4% from the bottom and right, **throughout the whole clip**. It preserves the dimensions and copies the audio unchanged; the video must be re-encoded, so minor compression changes are possible.

**Shorter or smaller?** That would reduce local processing time and file size, but not the credit cost—it’s already **zero**. No need to shorten or shrink your clip.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed
